document.summary: This site now renders Markdown in document bodies, compiled to HTML at build time.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: This document describes how Markdown is written and rendered in the documents on this site, and the choices behind it.

sections.title: Why
sections.content: Every document here is a JSON file, and each section carries a `content` string that used to be printed verbatim. That was fine while the documents were lists of contacts and keys. It stopped being fine with [L5Z12-PERSONAL-003](/document/L5Z12-PERSONAL-003), which is an article: it wants links in the middle of a sentence and endpoints set in monospace, and a plain-text renderer just prints the square brackets and the backticks at the reader.

sections.title: How it works
sections.content:
Section bodies are now Markdown, compiled to HTML while the site builds — by the same processor Astro uses for its own `.md` pages. Nothing changes for the reader: the pages are still static HTML, and no Markdown parser is shipped to the browser.

The document format is unchanged, so writing a section is still just writing a string:

```json
{
  "id": "notes",
  "number": 1,
  "title": "Notes",
  "content": "A paragraph with a [link](https://example.com) and `inline code`."
}
```

sections.title: What renders
sections.content:
CommonMark plus the GitHub extensions — **bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `inline code`, links, images, blockquotes, ordered and unordered lists, tables, footnotes and fenced code blocks.

Not every field is treated the same way, because not every field is a place where markup belongs:

| Where | Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Section body | Rendered to HTML |
| Summary on the index | Stripped to plain text |
| `<meta>` description, JSON-LD | Stripped to plain text |
| Markdown twin of the page | Passed through untouched |

The summaries are stripped rather than rendered because they sit inside the link that wraps each entry on [the index](/documents), and a link inside a link is not valid HTML.

sections.title: Choices
sections.content:
Three decisions are worth writing down:

- Headings inside a section body shift down two levels — a `#` becomes an `<h3>` — because the section title above it is already an `<h2>`. Prose cannot outrank the document it sits in.
- Links to other origins get `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer external"` on their own, matching the links written by hand elsewhere in the document. Site-relative links are left alone.
- Code blocks are not syntax-highlighted. A highlighter writes one theme's colours into inline styles, and inline styles cannot follow the light and dark toggle in the footer. Plain monospace on a bordered block is honest here, and it costs nothing.

sections.title: Markdown twins
sections.content: Every page is also published as Markdown: append `/index.md` to any path, such as [/document/L5Z12-PERSONAL-004/index.md](/document/L5Z12-PERSONAL-004/index.md). Those twins needed no work at all — the section bodies were already Markdown, so they pass straight through. The HTML is the derived form now, not the source.
